body:
**Chapter V3 - Session Management** 

Perfectly well done chapter! I got nothing to change, but one recommendation I have below.  

**Recommendation:** 

Credential Service Providers (CSPs) are not a very common term for many. I understand that in NIST-language this is a role and maybe we have to emphasize this on the top of this chapter first that some terms here are very much NIST-centric or related to NIST mainly so that any user who reads this chapter won't be misguided and confused with Credential Service Provider (CSP) vs Content-Security-Policy (CSP). Maybe we need to give a brief description of each NIST roles like how roles are defined in V51 OAuth 2.0 chapter. What do you all think?

comments.body: I agree @csfreak92 - how about we just use the standard term Identity Provider (IdP)? It's way more accepted and close enough.

> I agree [@csfreak92](https://github.com/csfreak92) - how about we just use the standard term Identity Provider (IdP)? It's way more accepted and close enough.

I like Identity Provider (IdP) more, @jmanico! I agree with it as it is widely used and quite common in security terms that people use. Do you want me to draft something for this or would you want to take a stab at it?
I think @elarlang and @tghosth should make that call. They have put a lot of work into v3.

I think that is a great comment and I would love to replace credential service provider with identity provider if you are convinced they are the same thing.

@csfreak92 if you are sure that we can do this replacement, please can you open a PR for that and include any changes to the glossary that are needed.

The are not exactly the same. A credential provider is usually a subset (a portion of) an identity provider. But I think they are close enough where the meaning of the requirements are not lost and are mostly improved for clarity.
Quick question @tghosth: do you want me to just update the glossary or glossary + usage of CSP in the V3 requirements where they were mentioned?

@tghosth, I did not remove CSP definitions in the Glossary. I kept it there so that whenever people refer to it as under NIST reference, they would understand it is for that context. 

Good reference from NIST says that IdPs are the other commonly used term for CSPs in page 11 of this guide: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ir/2018/NIST.IR.8149.pdf
I would like to leave this open to have a final review of the chapter texts here
